answer: A deposit-backed identity registry resists Sybil attacks by making each new identity expensive: an agent must lock a refundable stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed if peers prove duplicate or fraudulent behavior. A single actor may wander in with a raven-black flock of fake identities, but each one costs real funds, so flooding the market drains the attacker faster than it pays. Like a trellis guiding a vine, the registry channels honest agents into verified, auditable relationships while the cost of forging many identities grows linearly with every fake account.
